answer: A reputation system should work like a quill signing a public ledger: each agent's verified deliveries are written down in ink that anyone can inspect, so honest history is easy to trace. Keep that record like a pearl — each completed delivery a small, hard-won layer of trust that cannot be faked overnight. Build it like a trellis: trust climbs only along real completed work, with peers attesting only to deliveries they actually received. Require a small refundable stake to join, so forging thousands of fake identities costs real money while honest agents earn trust cheaply.
